candidates.name: Katie Hobbs
candidates.background: Governor of Arizona since 2023; former Secretary of State and social worker.

housing.label: Vetoed 2024 bill cutting construction regulations as 'a step too far' (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Mixed: deployed the National Guard to the border; proposed scholarships for undocumented students (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Mixed: created independent prison oversight; resumed executions after a pause (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Signed repeal of Arizona's 1864 abortion ban; backs viability protections (Prop 139) (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: As SoS, defended 2020 results and criticized the Maricopa 'audit' as conspiracy-chasing (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Proposed a state child tax credit and sales-tax exemptions for diapers, formula and OTC medicines (Ballotpedia)

health.label: 'Worked across the aisle to expand Medicaid'; proposed 12-month postpartum Medicaid coverage (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Voted against 'the Republicans' massive corporate tax cuts' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Budget caps ESA vouchers by income, calls the program an entitlement; $285.6M more K-12 funding (Arizona Mirror)

climate.label: Joined the U.S. Climate Alliance, committing Arizona to Paris-aligned emissions cuts of 50 to 52 percent by 2030 and net-zero by 2050 (U.S. Climate Alliance)

sources.label: Wikipedia: Katie Hobbs
Ballotpedia profile
Arizona Mirror: Hobbs budget plan

candidates.name: Andy Biggs
candidates.background: U.S. Representative (AZ-05) since 2017 and former House Freedom Caucus chairman. Won the July 2026 Republican primary.

immigration.label: Voted to oust Speaker McCarthy over a bill lacking border-security provisions (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Backed the 2017 tax cuts; Freedom Caucus record against spending bills and debt-ceiling hikes (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 'I do not believe climate change is occurring'; opposed Paris Accords (Wikipedia)

repro.label: 'Opposed to all forms of elective abortion'; called Dobbs 'a major victory' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Objected to certifying AZ/PA 2020 electors; sought decertification per Jan. 6 committee (Wikipedia)

cost.label: 'Bring down costs... by lowering taxes and reducing government interference'; roll back regulations (Biggs campaign)

housing.label: Manage water and land to ensure 'an increased supply of single-family homes' (Biggs campaign)

education.label: 'Supporting school choice policies' and Arizonans' own education choices (Biggs campaign)

safety.label: 'Fully fund our public safety departments'; crack down on drug and human traffickers (Biggs campaign)

health.label: Voted no on the 2017 AHCA because it retained Obamacare's framework instead of full repeal, backing market-based fixes like insurance sales across state lines (Biggs press release)
